doc: Which layer owns which paths, and which layers each may import. Checked by scripts/check-layers.ts (npm test). Guardrail-owned: change only under a guardrail-scoped work item (architecture/guardrails.json).

layers.name: core-contract
layers.doc: The wire contract as the host sees it, plus guest-side protocol support. Pure data and pure functions.

layers.name: core-kernel
layers.doc: The browser bridge. Browser mechanism only; knows no capability pack and no application.

layers.name: reference-engine
layers.doc: The TypeScript reference application engine. Application meaning; no browser mechanism.

layers.name: package-facade
layers.doc: The npm package's root entrypoint. Capability packs, federation and the reference engine are exported from their own subpaths, never from here.

layers.name: reference-demo
layers.doc: The repository's own demo page (index.html): its composition root and stylesheet. Not published (package.json files excludes dist/main.*); composes the kernel with the reference engine.

layers.name: capability-support
layers.doc: Shared mechanism for capability packs (opaque handle tables). Knows no capability; packs may import it, Core may not.

layers.name: host-adapter
layers.doc: Optional hosts: transports that run an engine somewhere (a .NET or raw WebAssembly module). Mechanism only; engine output is decoded with the generated codec. The composition root supplies loaders, so no computed import appears here.

layers.name: renderer
layers.doc: The optional server and static renderer (#38): reads template HTML, applies the same binding policy the kernel applies, and drives an engine on the server with browser-only capabilities explicitly absent. It may use the kernel's pure policy and handshake modules, never the BrowserKernel itself (test/renderer.test.ts holds its module closure to that). Never imported by Core.

layers.name: capability-pack
layers.doc: An optional browser capability. One instance per directory; packs never import each other or any application.

layers.name: tooling
layers.doc: Development and conformance tooling (fake host, trace, replay). Never imported by Core; test and diagnostic authority only.

externalImports.doc: Every layer above is in the published package, which has zero runtime dependencies: a bare or node: specifier is a violation.

engineLibraries.doc: Pure application-side libraries in any guest language. They may not acquire browser, JavaScript-interop, network, filesystem or process authority. A library that genuinely needs one is a host adapter and belongs elsewhere.

protocolForbiddenTypes.doc: Browser runtime objects never cross the boundary. No contract type may take one of these names, and no core-contract source may mention one.
